bug_semantics: Xext/sync.c FreeCounter sets beingDestroyed, then walks pCounter->sync.pTriglist calling pTrigger->CounterDestroyed on each node before taking pnext and free()ing the node. For an XSync Await, CounterDestroyed is SyncAwaitTriggerFired, which FreeResource()s the Await; FreeAwait then xfree/free()s the entire SyncAwaitUnion that holds every wait-condition SyncAwait. When several Await conditions reference the same counter, FreeAwait skips SyncDeleteTriggerFromSyncObject because beingDestroyed is already TRUE, so leftover list nodes still point at the now-freed SyncAwait objects. The next loop step therefore reads ptl->pTrigger (and can also lose a valid pnext) after the backing Await memory is gone (CWE-416). A local client that awaits multiple conditions on counters and has a second client destroy those counters can crash the X server or escalate if it runs as root. The 2026 patch uses nt_list_for_each_entry_safe, advances pTriglist before the callback, guards a NULL pTrigger, and NULLs remaining list pTrigger pointers from FreeAwait while the object is being destroyed.
flaw_origin: The FreeCounter destroy-iteration and the Await path that frees sibling SyncAwait structs first appear together in public xserver git as ded6147bfb5d75ff1e67c858040a628b61bc17d1 (2003-11-14, Kaleb Keithley, "R6.6 is the Xorg base-line"). That commit adds Xext/sync.c with FreeCounter looping for (ptl = pCounter->pTriglist; ptl; ptl = pnext) { (*ptl->pTrigger->CounterDestroyed)(ptl->pTrigger); pnext = ptl->next; xfree(ptl); }, FreeAwait skipping SyncDeleteTriggerFromCounter when pCounter->beingDestroyed is set, SyncAwaitTriggerFired calling FreeResource on the Await, and pAwait->trigger.CounterDestroyed = SyncAwaitTriggerFired. Immediate parent cb6ef07bf01e72d1a6e6e83ceb7f76d6534da941 has no Xext/sync.c (tree is only hw/). Later 1a99110f0c221b79045ea26d61c4a1ec1e0d7341 (ANSI prototypes), 9838b7032ea9792bec21af424c53c07078636d21 (indent), 99daf419a3070c347c0cd29b4a9bae07eca7bd6d / c66a410d378090f350beb398649e9d9262933785 (generic SyncObject), and 7f962c70b6d9c346477f23f6c15211e749110078 (wrap the same loop in if (initialized)) preserve the CounterDestroyed walk; they are not first-writes. The 2003 commit is a vendor import/baseline rather than a reconstructable squash of finer public members; no finer public object first writing these lines was found.

reasoning: Vulnerability first: the advisory names a FreeCounter use-after-free when a client awaits multiple conditions and another client destroys the counters. Pre-fix FreeCounter invokes CounterDestroyed per list node while FreeAwait, seeing beingDestroyed, does not unlink those nodes and instead frees the whole AwaitUnion; leftover pTrigger pointers then alias freed SyncAwait memory. The 2026 patch keeps the destroy walk but makes the list and pTrigger pointers valid across the callback, confirming the defect is that iterator plus the beingDestroyed skip. BIC: public history first writes FreeCounter's CounterDestroyed walk, the beingDestroyed skip in FreeAwait, and CounterDestroyed=SyncAwaitTriggerFired together in the 2003 Xorg R6.6 baseline that adds Xext/sync.c. Parent tree lacks the file, so parent absence is verified. Later initialized-guard, indent, and SyncObject-generic commits are not first-writes. The baseline is the smallest surviving public object; no finer public member reconstructing the same first-write was found.
